title: The effect of overheating · ET-SoC-1
description: What temperatures processors are built for and why the limits sit where they do; whether a limit should watch the average of the die or its hottest spot; whether heat changes how fast transistors switch; and why a chip that overheats stops and then works again when it cools. Outside research with numbered sources, checked on the ET-SoC-1: the firmware build of two of its cards throttles on the mean of 34 sensors, and on three of the four cards nothing acts once the clock is at 600 MHz, yet in two pre-registered experiments on aifoundry3 and aifoundry1 card 1 (E53) the hottest sensor ran only 1–3 °C above the mean, work per cycle at an 80–85 °C mean matched rest, and 663 exact-checked launches computed nothing wrong.
